scope: 40 whole exclusions inspected, with actual parent meanings/stances/access compared for consolidated components. Full final integration remains pending.
additional_source_basis: Prior complete source/current-record inspections, earlier auxiliary full-page rereads of 193, 197, 200, 203–204, 219, 221 and 241, and rendered map225 source-scope decision.

rows.review_disposition: 193 Goethe’s interpretation is coherently subordinate to Valmy’s military and historical significance. D319 retains the route explicitly; attribution does not require a separately weighted biography.

178 Clootz’s liberation propaganda belongs in war origins, whereas his election on 193 belongs to Convention composition. Bind both 18017 and 5F07 rather than implying a single war-origin parent fully preserves both phases.
Running headers and folios are furniture; substantive titles remain eligible.
Retire the chunk-nine ownership boundary as a whole-book exclusion: 195–196 and 220–221 are eligible source.

Bare forward pointers on 202/212/215/217 are navigation. The surrounding Vendée, British strategy, Italian and peace discussions remain eligible, as do the target treatments independently inspected elsewhere.

Campaign/coalition lists do not automatically generate personal or territorial biographies. Preserve independently useful role/aim differences and turning points; no whole chunk or class of actors is excluded.
Quotations can remain substantive policy/campaign/reception evidence without a separate biography of each speaker.
Bare note markers and omitted endnotes supply no eligible independent treatment; body text is unaffected.
Retire: 195–196 trial/execution are eligible in the whole book. Local ownership cannot remove their evidence.
Retire: 220–221 opening provincial-conflict discussion is eligible. This is division of source work, not a subject exclusion.
Running furniture and bare navigation are excluded only as regions; substantive cross-chapter content remains eligible.
Unavailable endnotes are excluded explicitly by the frozen policy and cannot establish source requirements.
Coalition names/subsidy recipients can be subordinate access, but different war aims remain essential. This does not exclude separately developed diplomacy or actors elsewhere.
War slogans and remarks provide evidence of intentions/perceptions. Exact textual reproduction is not a benchmark demand; their substantive meanings remain eligible.

Casualty and force totals explain scale, imbalance, losses and mobilization. They need no standalone numerical heading but remain qualified parent evidence, including nominal versus effective strength.

Correct the length-based threshold: a brief policy action may still provide useful personal access. Attribution alone does not compel independent weighting, and developed whole-book roles remain eligible.

The war-course umbrella is broader than AEC’s actual causal argument. Do not assert semantic equivalence. Retire only an additional generic chronological umbrella; preserve the causal conclusion in AEC and distinct campaign/diplomatic requirements under their separately reviewed subjects.

E1A main meaning explicitly retains treaty-less coalition formation, incompatible aims and the resulting opportunity for French survival. Coherent consolidation preserves the analytical disunity component.

81DD explicitly names Carnot, organization and differentiated national mobilization. Rebind to that August mobilization parent, not C79’s separate February levy; retain equipment/implementation and avoid a sole-hero theory of victory.

210 and 329D parent retain Spanish fear of limited subversion, advance of French troops and peace allowing redeployment. No extra weighted Spanish peace duplicate is needed; domestic resistance to invaders remains distinct from court fear.

214 and 9168 main meaning/access preserve four relief attempts, Rivoli, Mantua and the subsequent constrained advance on Vienna. These named turning points remain retrievable within the coherent campaign.
Running furniture/page numbers are excluded; the substantive chapter title and text on the listed pages remain eligible.

225 interior symbols, legend, regions and routes are excluded semantic regions by the frozen policy. Replace the claimed semantic permission; only the literal substantive caption may support the revised 9DA subject.
221 personal appearance/relationship detail is subordinate; preserve Roland-circle political sociability and the fact Buzot would soon become her lover, rather than a fully contemporaneous assertion.
221 Philippe-Égalité allegation is polemical inference, not established intent. Its political function remains eligible.
241 English pay is explicitly possible; command and royalist affiliation are treated differently. Preserve Caen military and political division access.
Local leaders, towns and clubs may be subordinate to developed movements. Briefness does not exclude any unique mechanism or useful access, and no whole listed page is rejected.
Contested estimates and official/revised counts need qualifications, not automatic truth or removal. Preserve exaggerated revolt geography, notional forces and ratification distinctions as evidence.
Economic examples have distinct causal roles in supply crisis and particular cities. Separate commodity headings are optional, but local trade/subsistence differences must survive.
Independent retrieval significance can justify a personal requirement even in brief treatment; attribution alone need not. Retain the conditional rule without a sustained-length prerequisite.

225 cartographic labels/regions/symbolic routes cannot establish semantic requirements under frozen scope. This corrects the historical semantic-permission record, preserving caption-only eligibility and independently supported prose routes.
Slogans and insults carry political stance/mobilization content. They need not be separate textual subjects; paraphrased meanings remain eligible.
Dates normally identify events, and conventional date-named events may provide access. Preserve chronology and the source’s genuine conflicts rather than silently choosing one.
232 captured towns locate Vendéan expansion and possible access to sea/Loire. Preserve campaign directions and strategic stakes under the campaign; do not infer them from excluded map225.

Authorial disagreements with historians, including inflated federalist extent, are substantive stance. No unspecified historian biography is required, but the interpretive correction must remain explicit.
Running heads, bare chapter numerals and folios are excluded furniture; source semantics and density protocols remain separate.

232/243/246 substantiate simultaneous frontier defeats, internal war, provincial challenge and delayed constitutional implementation. CC141 can contain this component only if parent meaning/stance retain the mutually reinforcing crisis, not merely a generic institution list.
221/236 and 86D parent retain loose Girondin circles and opposition to modern party/government assumptions. Preserve the non-party distinction in final main fields.

229/236/237 and 86D parent retain Montagnard practical adaptation and already established predominance. No new duplicate is needed, but June purge must not be described as overthrow of a Girondin government.

65D main meaning/access explicitly retain sectional/National Guard coercion, Paris divisions and opposing uses of sections. This is coherent within national sovereignty while broader social sansculotte identity remains separately accessible.
